name: Funerary Tradition in the Prehistory of Sardinia – The domus de janas
description: Across Sardinia, prehistoric communities carved about 3,500 "fairy houses" (domus de janas) into solid rock as tombs, mostly between 3400 and 2700 BCE. Their chambers mimic the rooms of real homes, with some walls bearing spirals, bull's horns and false doors, and traces of red ochre. Anghelu Ruju near Alghero and Sant'Andrea Priu at Bonorva are among the best places to step inside.
